reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and the cited text supports it: 20.1 gives a full Vendor defend/indemnify obligation for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, and 20.2 adds Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud — matching the preferred position.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity (20.3) is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised; Customer's violation of Applicable Law) with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions, so no one-sided exposure to narrow.

Standard indemnity procedure is present and balanced (20.4 notice/cooperation/control with prejudice-limited notice failure and consent for adverse settlements), and 20.5 supplies the usual IP remedies in addition to, not in lieu of, defence.

Vendor's indemnity is not squeezed by the liability cap because indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, which is better than the fallback 3x super-cap; the narrow cap base is correctly deferred to the limitation-of-liability rule rather than double-flagged here.
No redline or counterparty comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding, and the deterministic check (vendor IP indemnity present) corroborates the classification.
